Issued at 243 PM EDT Wed Sep 16 2026

Today-tonight... Upper level high pressure across the Deep South 
will move ever so slightly to the east today, with shortwave energy 
traversing across Florida through the period. At the surface,  high 
pressure along the eastern seaboard of the US will slowly shift 
eastward, while the axis remains over the Florida peninsula.
Locally, the pressure gradient will remain tight, resulting in 
breezy and gusty east-northeast winds of 15-20 mph with peak gusts 
25-30 mph at times. A drier airmass has filtered across north-
central Florida today, with GOES-19 ECONUS Total Precipitable Water 
satellite image showing PW values ranging from 1.2-1.7" from Orlando 
Metro northward, and 2.0"+ southward. The rain chances reflect this, 
with a low to medium (20-40 percent) chance generally around the 
Orlando Metro area and north and west of the I-4 corridor, with a 
medium to high (50-80 percent) chance southward. A few storms will 
be possible throughout the day. However, moist low level onshore 
flow should keep at least an isolated mention along the Volusia 
coast through this afternoon. Storms today will be capable of 
producing occasional to frequent lightning strikes, gusty winds of 
40-45 mph, and heavy downpours. Any lingering activity across the 
interior will diminish into early evening, with isolated to 
scattered showers and storms remaining possible along the coast in 
the onshore flow through the overnight hours, with greatest coverage 
forecast to occur along the southern Treasure Coast. 

Outside of storms, temperatures are forecast to be seasonable, with 
afternoon highs in the upper 80s to low 90s. These temperatures 
combined with high humidity will produce peak heat indices of 100-
107F. Warm and muggy conditions will continue tonight, with 
overnight lows in the mid to upper 70s, remaining warmest along the 
coast. 

At the beaches, a high risk of life threatening rip currents exist 
at all area beaches today, along with rough surf. Heed the advice of 
lifeguards, beach patrol flags, and signs. Entering the surf is not 
advised! There is also hazardous marine conditions across all 
central Florida Atlantic Waters. See Marine section for more
details. 

Thursday... Upper level high pressure across the Deep South will 
remain in place, with shortwave energy traversing across Florida 
through the day. An upper level trough will develop offshore the 
east coast of Florida on Thursday and slowly shift westwards towards 
the Florida peninsula through the day. At the surface,  high 
pressure along the eastern seaboard of the US will slowly shift 
eastward and offshore by late Thursday, while the axis remains over 
the Florida peninsula. Locally, breezy conditions will remain as 
east-northeast winds of 10-15 mph with gusts to around 20 mph at 
times are forecast through the day. Drier air continues to filter 
across the local area, limiting convection north and west of the I-4 
corridor. Multiple rounds of more widely scattered showers and a few 
storms remain forecast mostly south of the I-4 corridor. Greatest 
coverage (PoP 40-60 percent) will be Cape Canaveral southward and 
towards Lake Okeechobee. Much like today, any lingering activity 
across the interior will diminish into early evening, with isolated 
to scattered showers and storms remaining possible along the coast 
in the onshore flow through the overnight hours, with greatest 
coverage forecast to occur along the southern Treasure Coast.   

Temperatures will be seasonable, with afternoon highs in the upper 
80s to low 90s. Muggy and warm conditions will continue overnight 
and into early morning, with lows in the mid to upper 70s. However, 
areas along the Barrier Islands may struggle to fall below the 80 
degree mark each morning.

Friday-Tuesday... Upper level high pressure across the Deep South 
will remain in place through the weekend. The aforementioned trough 
will become a closed low off the eastern coast of Florida on Friday 
and slowly push westward, across the Florida peninsula, and out into 
the Gulf through the weekend before shifting northward towards the 
LA/MS/AL coastline into early next week. At the surface, high 
pressure in the western Atlantic will slowly move north and westward 
(closer to the US) through the period, with the axis remaining over 
the Florida peninsula. Locally, moisture will recover behind the low 
pressure, resulting in moderate to high rain chances areawide into 
early next week. Light easterly winds veer southeast to south late 
in the weekend, becoming more onshore and locally enhanced each 
afternoon with the development of a weak sea breeze. Temperatures 
will be seasonable with afternoon highs in the upper 80s to low 90s 
and overnight lows in the mid to upper 70s.
